_comment: Room control surfaces. A DESIGN says what the surface looks like and where it sits; SECTIONS say what goes in it; a section's FILTER says which of the room's entities qualify. A card can populate every device in a room and let configuration narrow it — that is what `source: "all"` plus a filter is for. Three layers merge (house -> floor -> room), sections by id, so one room overriding one row inherits everything else.

sheet.label: Bottom sheet
sheet.description: Slides up from the bottom over the plan. The default: reachable one-handed on a phone, and it never covers the room you just tapped.

rail.label: Side rail
rail.description: A drawer down one edge. Good on a tablet in landscape, where a bottom sheet wastes the short axis.

dock.label: Docked panel
dock.description: Sits BESIDE the plan rather than over it, so the plan stays visible and stays interactive. On a wide screen this is the one that uses the empty space either side of a square floor plan.

popover.label: Popover at the room
popover.description: A small card anchored to the room you tapped. Least disruptive, but only fits a handful of controls — pair it with a tight filter.

bar.label: Compact bar
bar.description: A single strip across the bottom. Room name, a few group buttons, nothing else. For rooms where you only ever hit All on / All off.

grid.label: Tile grid
grid.description: Everything in the room as equal tiles, no section headings. Reads like a dashboard page rather than a control sheet — best with `source: "all"`.

fullscreen.label: Full screen
fullscreen.description: Takes the whole viewport. For a room with a lot in it, or for a wall-mounted tablet where the plan is not the point once you have chosen a room.

_shortcuts_comment: SHORTCUTS are the user's own actions, and the builder has no vocabulary of its own for them. A shortcut is a label plus something to do: an entity to toggle, a scene to activate, a script to run with variables, or a service call written out. What it MEANS — do-not-disturb, turbo, movie night, holiday mode — is the label, and belongs to the house, not to this file. They live on `project.shortcuts`, `floor.shortcuts` and `room.shortcuts` and accumulate across the three, so a house shortcut appears in every room and a room's appears in one. `slot: "header"` puts one in the panel's button row; anything else lands in the section named by `section` (default `shortcuts`). Nothing here is created in Home Assistant: a shortcut only ever references an entity or service that already exists.

shortcutSchema.id: unique within its layer; used to override or hide an inherited shortcut from a nearer one
shortcutSchema.label: what the button says
shortcutSchema.entity: the entity it acts on. Alone, its domain decides what a tap does — see domainActions below
shortcutSchema.service: domain.service to call instead of the domain default, e.g. script.turn_on
shortcutSchema.data: extra service data, e.g. {"speed": 3} for a script that takes variables
shortcutSchema.state: the entity that decides whether the button looks lit; defaults to `entity`
shortcutSchema.section: which section it lands in when slot is section (default: shortcuts)
shortcutSchema.confirm: true to ask before running it
shortcutSchema.enabled: false to hide one inherited from a further layer

_domainActions_comment: What a tap DOES, and which widget an entity gets, BY DOMAIN — Home Assistant's vocabulary, not any one house's. This is the registry that replaces a switch statement in every backend: the card, the editor preview and the marker tap all ask the same question here. `control` picks the widget (toggle | button | number | select | text | readout); `tap` is the primary service; `alt` is what a hold offers where a hold means something other than more-info; `set` is how a value widget writes back. `onRule` answers “is this on”, the same question the library asks of a marker — `on` (the default), `notOff`, `numeric`, or `momentary` for a scene or a button that has no on-state at all. Where a domain's off-states are simply a list of words (`closed`, `locked`, `idle`), say so with `offStates` instead; it beats `onRule` and needs no new rule name.

camera._comment: A camera is not a switch. With no entry here it fell through to the default toggle, so tapping one called camera.toggle. It names no `tap` service on purpose: the runtime falls back to more-info when a domain declares none, and more-info on a camera IS the live stream.

_filter_comment: Every key is optional and they AND together. Omit the lot and the section shows whatever its source produced. `include` is applied after everything else and always wins, so one stubborn entity can be forced back in without loosening the whole filter.

filterSchema.domains: array of entity domains to keep, e.g. ["light","switch"]
filterSchema.kinds: array of marker kinds to keep: fixture | device | furniture
filterSchema.types: array of library type ids to keep, e.g. ["spot","tube"]
filterSchema.excludeTypes: array of library type ids to drop
filterSchema.deviceClasses: array of device_class values to keep
filterSchema.shortcuts: array of shortcut ids to keep — only ever matches candidates that came from the shortcuts source
filterSchema.match: text matched against entity id and friendly name. May be an ARRAY — any one matching keeps the candidate. The token "@room" expands to the room's own match keys (room.keys, else its id and name), which is how one shipped section serves every room.
filterSchema.matchMode: contains | word | regex   (default: contains). In `word` mode a needle ending in `_` is a plain prefix test, because requiring a boundary after "gr_" would demand a second underscore right where the entity id's next word starts.
filterSchema.entityPattern: regex the entity id must match, e.g. "^script\\.my_home_" to scope a namespace
filterSchema.excludePattern: regex on the entity id that drops it, e.g. "^scene\\.internal_" for automation-internal scenes nobody should tap
filterSchema.exclude: array of entity ids to drop outright
filterSchema.include: array of entity ids to force in, applied last
filterSchema.hideUnavailable: drop entities with no state, or unavailable/unknown
filterSchema.onlyControllable: drop types the library marks readOnly
filterSchema.limit: keep at most N after sorting; 0 = no limit

header._buttons_note: Four built-ins, and that is all the framework has an opinion about. Everything else in this row is a SHORTCUT the house defined — a do-not-disturb boolean, a turbo switch, a goodnight scene — placed here with `slot: "header"`. They are appended in order after these, or wherever `order` puts them.

sections.label: Brightness
sections._note: Drives every dimmable light the filter keeps.

sections.label: Groups
sections._note: One button per fixture type present. groupBy 'group' honours a fixture's own `group` override, which is how a marker drawn as a spot can be kept out of the room's Spots button.

sections.label: Sensors
sections._note: Off by default — most rooms do not need their motion sensor as a button. Turn it on for a room where the readings matter.

sections.label: Scenes
sections._note: Two ways in, on purpose. A scene the house made a SHORTCUT of is named and always shows. A scene MATCHED from the catalogue costs no configuration at all and picks up the ones you add later — matched with word boundaries, because 'informal' literally contains 'formal' and that crossed two rooms' scenes in the hand-written version. Give a room `keys: ["guest_room", "gr_"]` when its entities are named after something other than the room's own id.
sections._extending: Scripts are deliberately NOT keyword-matched here: a bare `script.` would drag in every unrelated script with a room word in its name. Scope them to your own namespace by adding a third source — {"source":"catalogue","filter":{"domains":["script"],"entityPattern":"^script\\.my_home_","match":"@room","matchMode":"word"}} — and drop automation-internal scenes with an `excludePattern` such as "^scene\\.internal_".

sections.label: Automations
sections._note: Off by default: an automation is something you occasionally disable, not something you reach for daily. Tapping one enables or disables it; holding runs it.

sections.label: Shortcuts
sections._note: Where a shortcut lands unless it named another section or asked for the header — plus any logic marker standing in the room. The two rows above skim the scenes and automations off this one, so a house that puts everything in `shortcuts` still gets them sorted; a house that wants one undivided row turns those two off. Sorted by the order they were written, because the person who wrote them chose it.

sections.label: Everything here
sections._note: Populates every entity bound to anything in this room. This is the 'show it all and let the filter narrow it' section — set a filter rather than hand-listing.

sections.label: More
sections._note: Hand-picked entities with no marker on the plan — an AC's Eco/Turbo switch, a room's humidifier.

logic._note: The room as a control panel rather than a light switch — for a room where what you actually reach for is a mood or a shortcut, not an individual downlight.
